fact_text: Total cash dividends paid by KSE-100 companies were about PKR 230 billion in 2016, according to the presenter's data.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Retiring at 60? How to Manage Your Money for the Next 25 Years' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dividends are linked to company profits rather than to the share price, so dividend income can stay steadier than the share price through periods of volatility.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Retiring at 60? How to Manage Your Money for the Next 25 Years' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Holding a basket of about 10-12 dividend-paying stocks means a dividend cut at one company can be offset by increases at others, which the presenter treats as the main protection against policy changes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Retiring at 60? How to Manage Your Money for the Next 25 Years' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter applies a 15% tax to dividend income when calculating after-tax yield from dividend-paying stocks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Retiring at 60? How to Manage Your Money for the Next 25 Years' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter treats PSX dividend-paying stocks as able to yield around 8% gross, or about 7% after the 15% dividend tax, which he uses to compare them with rental property.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Retiring at 60? How to Manage Your Money for the Next 25 Years' (YouTube transcript, undated)
